yeoju.historicalWeight: Yeoju carries Joseon royal memory through King Sejong's tomb and river-side temple culture around Silleuksa. Its position along the Namhan River makes it a natural first threshold after leaving Seoul's density.
yeoju.modernIdentity: Today Yeoju also works as a Seoul-adjacent escape with ceramics, outlet shopping, riverside leisure, and a softer suburban-to-regional rhythm before the trip commits to deeper inland movement.
yeoju.routeMeaning: Yeoju is a junction city because it can send the traveler south-inland toward Chungju or east-inland toward Wonju. It should read as the first place where Seoul loosens and the route has a real choice.
yeoju.imageBrief: Use Namhan River, Silleuksa or royal-tomb imagery, ceramics or outlet-present-day cues, and a map that shows the split toward Chungju and Wonju.

gangneung.historicalWeight: Gangneung carries old east-coast culture through Gyeongpo, Ojukheon, pavilions, markets, and beach-town memory. It is where the mountain crossing from the interior finally becomes a sea-facing city.
gangneung.modernIdentity: Today Gangneung is also coffee streets, rail access, hotels, beaches, seafood, festivals, and one of Korea's strongest coast-city brands for English-speaking travelers.
gangneung.routeMeaning: Gangneung is a junction city because Route 2 can end here as the mountain-to-sea payoff, while Route 4 can continue south along National Route 7 toward Donghae, Samcheok, and Busan.
gangneung.imageBrief: Use one mountain-to-sea arrival cue, one coffee or beach cue, one Ojukheon or Gyeongpo memory cue, and a map that shows the split between stopping in Gangneung and continuing down Route 4.

cheonan.historicalWeight: Cheonan works as the first southern control point out of Seoul. Independence-memory sites, station movement, and its long corridor role make it useful before routes split into different versions of central and southern Korea.
cheonan.modernIdentity: Modern Cheonan is a practical junction city with station hotels, Cheonan-Asan mobility, university energy, walnut snack identity, and enough services to soften the first hour out of Seoul.
cheonan.routeMeaning: Cheonan is a junction city because it can support Route 1 as the first southbound reset toward Busan and Route 5 as the first pacing stop before Gongju, Jeonju, Gwangju, Suncheon, and Yeosu. It closes the Seoul departure gap without stealing attention from the deeper regional chapters.
cheonan.imageBrief: Use station or Cheonan-Asan mobility, walnut snack or local food, independence-memory cues, and a map that shows the split toward Route 1 and Route 5.

daejeon.historicalWeight: Daejeon carries central-corridor history through rail movement, wartime displacement, science-city growth, and the practical geography that lets several versions of southbound Korea split cleanly.
daejeon.modernIdentity: Modern Daejeon is station efficiency, Yuseong hot-spring recovery, research and science-city identity, Sungsimdang bakery pilgrimage, food streets, hotels, and practical onward movement toward either the inland Busan line or the Honam land-end route.
daejeon.routeMeaning: Daejeon is a junction city because Route 1 can use it as the clean central reset toward Daegu and Busan, while Route 8 uses it as the stabilizing first southbound chapter before Jeonju, Gwangju, Mokpo, and Haenam.
daejeon.imageBrief: Use Daejeon Station, Yuseong recovery, science-city cues, Sungsimdang or central bakery streets, and a map that shows the split between the inland Busan route and the Honam land-end route.

jeonju.historicalWeight: Jeonju carries Jeolla food culture, hanok streets, old-city memory, markets, and regional identity strong enough to anchor both the Yeosu route and the deeper Honam land-end route.
jeonju.modernIdentity: Modern Jeonju is Hanok Village, bibimbap, makgeolli streets, market food, boutique stays, cafes, and one of the easiest regional Korea entry points for English-speaking travelers.
jeonju.routeMeaning: Jeonju is a junction city because Route 5 uses it as the warm inland food chapter before Gwangju, Suncheon, and Yeosu, while Route 8 uses it as the first deep Jeolla emotional chapter before Gwangju, Mokpo, and Haenam.
jeonju.imageBrief: Use Hanok Village, food streets, makgeolli, markets, and a map that shows Jeonju continuing either to the Route 5 south-coast finale or the Route 8 land-end descent.

gwangju.historicalWeight: Gwangju carries one of Korea's defining modern democratic-history chapters through May 18 memory, civic courage, Honam identity, and the relationship between city culture and political memory.
gwangju.modernIdentity: Modern Gwangju is Asia Culture Center, Mudeungsan, Yangnim-dong, markets, food, art, universities, and a metropolitan Honam stay that can send travelers toward Suncheon and Yeosu or toward Mokpo and Haenam.
gwangju.routeMeaning: Gwangju is a junction city because Route 5 uses it as the modern-history anchor before Suncheon and Yeosu, while Route 8 uses it as the civic-history center before Mokpo harbor and Haenam land-end symbolism.
gwangju.imageBrief: Use May 18 memory, Asia Culture Center, Mudeungsan, food streets, and a map that shows the split toward Route 5 ecology/night sea or Route 8 harbor/land end.

mokpo.historicalWeight: Mokpo carries southwest port memory, modern harbor history, Yudalsan, Gatbawi, ferries, and the island-facing geography that makes the city both an ending and a beginning.
mokpo.modernIdentity: Modern Mokpo is seafood, ferries, cable-car views, harbor walks, island departures, and Dadohae access. It can finish the West Sea route or launch the south-coast route toward Haenam and Wando.
mokpo.routeMeaning: Mokpo is a junction city because Route 6 ends here as the West Sea modern-port finale, Route 7 begins here as the gateway into Dadohae and the south coast, and Route 8 uses it as the harbor hinge before Haenam land-end symbolism.
mokpo.imageBrief: Use Yudalsan, Gatbawi, harbor food, ferry movement, Dadohae island cues, and a map that shows Route 6 ending, Route 7 beginning, and Route 8 finishing its harbor-to-land-end movement.

haenam.historicalWeight: Haenam carries southern land-end imagination through Ttangkkeut, Duryunsan, Daeheungsa, rural roads, temple memory, seafood, and the feeling of reaching the peninsula edge.
haenam.modernIdentity: Modern Haenam is land-end travel, Duryunsan views, Daeheungsa, seafood, slow rural stays, and the practical continuation toward Wando, Cheongsando, and Dadohae island travel.
haenam.routeMeaning: Haenam is a junction city because Route 8 can end here as the Seoul-to-Honam land-end finale, while Route 7 can continue from here toward Wando, Boseong, Suncheon, Yeosu, Hallyeohaesang, and Busan.
haenam.imageBrief: Use Ttangkkeut, Duryunsan, Daeheungsa, rural road/seafood cues, and a map that shows Haenam as Route 8 finale and Route 7 continuation toward Wando.

suncheon.historicalWeight: Suncheon carries old bay, reed-field, temple-region, and market-town memory before the route turns fully into the southern coast. Its landscape has always been about wetlands, fields, and controlled movement toward the sea.
suncheon.modernIdentity: Modern Suncheon is Suncheon Bay Wetland, Suncheon Bay National Garden, eco-travel, bird habitat, calmer stays, and a practical junction between Jeolla inland travel and the south-coast route.
suncheon.routeMeaning: Suncheon is a junction city because Route 5 uses it as the ecological hinge before the Yeosu finale, while Route 7 uses it as the point where the Dadohae-side west/south coast begins moving toward Yeosu, Namhae, Hallyeohaesang, Tongyeong, Geoje, and Busan.
suncheon.imageBrief: Use Suncheon Bay Wetland, National Garden, reeds, garden city cues, and a map that shows the split between the Route 5 Yeosu finale and the Route 7 eastward south-coast continuation.

yeosu.historicalWeight: Yeosu carries island-harbor memory, naval geography, Hyangiram, Odongdo, Dolsan, Expo-era modernization, seafood, and the emotional night-sea identity of Korea's southern coast.
yeosu.modernIdentity: Modern Yeosu is night sea, harbor lights, seafood, island walks, Dolsan Bridge, Expo-area services, ferries, and one of the most legible south-coast city brands for English-speaking travelers.
yeosu.routeMeaning: Yeosu is a junction city because Route 5 can finish here as the emotional south-coast payoff, while Route 7 continues through Yeosu into Namhae, Hallyeohaesang, Tongyeong, Geoje, and Busan. It is both a finale and a launch point.
yeosu.imageBrief: Use Yeosu night sea, Odongdo, Hyangiram, Dolsan Bridge, seafood, harbor lights, and a map that shows Yeosu as the Route 5 endpoint and Route 7 continuation.

busan.historicalWeight: Busan carries port history, wartime refuge memory, hillside neighborhoods, markets, beaches, maritime trade, and the role of a final harbor for several different versions of Korea travel.
busan.modernIdentity: Modern Busan is a major harbor city with beaches, markets, film culture, cafes, seafood, rail and ferry access, and enough scale to receive the inland route, the east-coast National Route 7 line, and the south-coast Hallyeohaesang line.
busan.routeMeaning: Busan is a junction city because Route 1 reaches it through inland heritage, Route 4 reaches it down the East Sea and National Route 7 coast, and Route 7 reaches it after Dadohae, Hallyeohaesang, Geoje, and the southern island road. The city should read as a finale with different emotional approaches.
busan.imageBrief: Use harbor, Jagalchi, beaches, hillside neighborhoods, night coast, and a map that shows the three major approaches into Busan: inland, east coast, and south coast.
